tips.title: Selecting the Right Paint for Model Kits
tips.text: Choose acrylic paints like Vallejo Model Air or Model Color for most applications due to their ease of use, adhesion, and drying times. For enamel-based paints like Tamiya Acrylics or Humbrol, use them for their durability and longevity. Lacquers like Alclad II are ideal for metallic finishes due to their high gloss and durability. Always use the recommended thinner for each paint type.

tips.title: Choosing the Right Sandpaper Grits for Each Stage
tips.text: For initial surface preparation, use coarse 120-180 grit sandpaper to remove mold seams and flash. For smoothing putty or filler, use medium 220-320 grit. For final sanding before painting, use fine 400-600 grit to achieve a smooth surface. Wet/dry sandpaper from brands like Tamiya or Norton provides better control and reduced dust.

tips.title: Filling Gaps with Vallejo Plastic Putty
tips.text: Vallejo Plastic Putty is ideal for filling gaps due to its lightweight, fast-drying formula. Apply a thin layer with a brush or palette knife, allowing it to dry completely. Sand with progressively finer grits, starting with 220 grit, then 320, and finally 400 grit before painting. Avoid using super glue and baking soda mixture as it can create bubbles and is harder to sand.

tips.title: Photo-Etch vs Resin Detail Parts
tips.text: For intricate details, photo-etch (PE) from brands like Eduard or ICM is superior. PE offers fine details not achievable with plastic or resin. For complex shapes and heavy details, resin parts from brands like MiniArt or Arma Hobby excel. Choose based on the level of detail and complexity required. PE is better for intricate, thin details, while resin is better for complex, heavy details.

tips.title: Choosing the Right Decal Setting Solutions
tips.text: For most applications, use Microscale Micro Set/Sol for decal setting. Micro Set helps decals slide into position, while Micro Sol softens the decal film for better adherence. For stubborn decals, use Mr. Mark Softer or Citadel Decal Medium. Apply sparingly with a fine brush, working from the center outwards to avoid creating bubbles. Always follow the manufacturer's instructions.
